title: rings: default nsize
purpose: Exercises `rings` [@epsrmanual], which counts closed rings of bonded molecules with the shortest-path criterion of Franzblau [@franzblau1991] (as cited in `chains_sp_criterion.f`): a ring is accepted only if no shorter path through the network connects two of its members. Bonds are defined as in `chains` (three distance windows and an angle), and histograms of neighbour numbers and ring sizes are written. This case checks the computed default ring length.
system: Analysed configuration: `200DMSO400Water.ato`, an unchanged copy of the EPSR-test box of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO; atom types S, O, C, H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1): 3200 atoms, DMSO mole fraction 1/3, 300 K, cubic box of side 33.1213 Å (0.0881 atoms/Å³), the EPSR model of the deuterated DMSO-water neutron data (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), cf. [@soperluzar1992]. Water O1-H1···O* hydrogen bonds to either a water or a DMSO oxygen acceptor (O-H 0.8-1.2, O···O 2.4-3.3, H···O 1.4-2.6 Å, angle <= 35°). The README reports 59 rings; the reference `fort.14` gives a mean neighbour number of 2.25 and a mean ring size of 4.85.
inputs: `ow.RINGS.dat`: one ring definition, `nsumt 0`, no `nsize` or `ndist`. `200DMSO400Water.ato` copied unchanged from EPSR-test; the keyword file was written by hand (the Fortran program creates no template when the named file does not exist; keywords and defaults from `setup_symbols_generic.f`).
verification: `repeat 2`, `nsumt 0`. `nsize` and `ndist` are not given, so the computed default `nsize` = `mring` = 25 ("Maximum ring length (max 25)") of `setup_symbols_rings` is used, as seen in the rewritten `.dat` of the reference (`nsize 25`, `ndist 1`, `nsumt 2`). Compared after each pass: `ow.RINGS.n01`, `ow.RINGS.dat`, `fort.14`. The configuration is the same in every pass, so the chained passes test the read-back of the accumulated file and the running-average arithmetic.
